C-INTERNATIONAL-TERMINOLOGY.Summary: Apply the agreed international terminology in the Russian portal's sources and reconcile both portal editions with the shared reference and governing vocabulary.

Goals.Goal: Use fixed international names consistently in visible content, navigation, diagrams, search and term definitions.
Preserve equivalent functional meaning and permitted language variants across the English and Russian sources.

Constraints.Constraint: Authority: the user explicitly requested replacement of Russian translated fixed terms by the agreed international names and alignment of both sites with both vocabularies. Reuse that authorization for source corrections, necessary projection fixes and verification.
Charter and other corpus sources own their content; generated HTML is regenerated, never manually patched.

Preserve decision rights, commitments, states, record identities, dates, legal entity names, external document titles and language neutrality. Russian explanatory definitions and the shared reference's Russian-language names remain in Russian.
Preserve unrelated working-tree changes and approved bundles. Apply only fixed forms required by the shared reference; do not force all permitted language variants into English.

NonGoals.NonGoal: New terminology policy, invented translations, changes to unrelated portals, commit, push or deployment.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Russian reader-facing uses of fixed terms agree with the shared reference, with documented explanatory or exact-title exceptions.
English and Russian pages preserve governing meanings and use consistent defined names.
All generated language routes, links, diagrams and searches work; source and repeatability checks pass.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Whole-site terminology sweep, paired source review and desktop/mobile browser checks.
